name: Rajasthan
tagline: Land of Kings, Forts and the Thar Desert
overview: Rajasthan, India's largest state by area, is a living museum of royal heritage. Its landscape sweeps from the golden Thar Desert to the Aravalli hills, dotted with hilltop forts, palaces reflected in lakes, and painted havelis. The Rajput legacy shows up in architecture, miniature painting, folk music and a fiercely colourful dress sense.
culture: Ghoomar and Kalbeliya folk dances, puppet (kathputli) theatre, blue pottery, block printing, and Manganiyar desert music define Rajasthani culture. Turbans and mirror-worked ghagras carry regional meaning.
history: Home to the Rajput clans from the 8th century, Rajasthan was a patchwork of princely states — Mewar, Marwar, Amber, Jaisalmer — that resisted and negotiated with Mughal and later British power, leaving behind an extraordinary density of forts and palaces.

name: Punjab
tagline: Land of Five Rivers and the Golden Temple
overview: Punjab is the spiritual heart of Sikhism and India's breadbasket. Its culture is warm, loud and generous — bhangra and giddha at every celebration, langar (free community meals) at every gurdwara, and mustard fields stretching to the horizon.
culture: Bhangra and giddha dance, Phulkari embroidery, Sufi and Gurbani music, and a food culture of makki di roti, sarson da saag and lassi. Hospitality (seva) is a defining value.
history: Shaped by the Indus civilisation, the Sikh Gurus, the empire of Maharaja Ranjit Singh, and the trauma of the 1947 Partition, Punjab's identity blends devotion, resilience and celebration.

name: Uttar Pradesh
tagline: Heartland of the Ganga, Nawabs and the Taj
overview: Uttar Pradesh holds India's most iconic monument (the Taj Mahal), its holiest river city (Varanasi), and the refined Nawabi culture of Lucknow. It is a dense weave of Mughal, Awadhi and ancient Hindu and Buddhist heritage.
culture: Kathak dance was born here; so were chikankari embroidery, thumri music, and the courtly tehzeeb (etiquette) of Lucknow. Varanasi's ghats host the daily Ganga aarti.
history: From the ancient kingdoms of Kashi and Kosala, through the Mughals at Agra and the Nawabs of Awadh, to a central role in 1857 and the freedom movement, UP has been at the centre of Indian history for millennia.

name: Bihar
tagline: Cradle of Buddhism, Jainism and ancient learning
overview: Bihar is where the Buddha attained enlightenment and where the world's first great university, Nalanda, once taught thousands. It is a land of profound spiritual and intellectual heritage along the Ganga plains.
culture: Madhubani (Mithila) painting, Chhath Puja devotion to the Sun, Bhojpuri and Maithili folk traditions, and the Sujani embroidery of Mithila define Bihar's cultural life.
history: The Mauryan and Gupta empires ruled from Pataliputra (modern Patna). Bodh Gaya, Nalanda, Vaishali and Rajgir made ancient Bihar (Magadha) a global centre of religion, philosophy and science.

name: Delhi
tagline: Eight cities, one capital — layers of empire
overview: Delhi is India's capital and one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities. It has been built and rebuilt at least eight times, leaving Mughal red-sandstone forts beside colonial boulevards and a thriving contemporary metropolis.
culture: A cosmopolitan blend of Mughal courtly heritage, Punjabi refugee energy after Partition, street food culture from Chandni Chowk to Nizamuddin, and qawwali at the Sufi shrines.
history: From the Tomars and Chauhans, through the Delhi Sultanate and the Mughals (who built Shahjahanabad), to the British capital of New Delhi designed by Lutyens, Delhi's stones record eight centuries of power.
